title: Two-Dimensional Kinematics
learning_objectives: Add and subtract vectors graphically and analytically, and use the result for velocity.
Analyse projectile motion: the horizontal and the vertical motion handled separately.
Work out the range, the maximum height and the time of flight of a projectile.

sections.title: Introduction to Two-Dimensional Kinematics
objectives: Describe what changes when motion is no longer along a straight line.

misconceptions.claim: Motion in two dimensions is just motion in one dimension done twice.
misconceptions.correction: Two dimensional motion is described by two coordinates, and the two of them follow separate rules.

summary: Two dimensional motion needs two coordinates, usually x and y.
The horizontal and the vertical motion are handled separately.
The reason is that gravity acts only in the vertical direction.
sections.no_worked_example_reason: The source carries no worked example for this section and no solved exercise to promote, so the practice is left to the exercises themselves.

sections.title: Kinematics in Two Dimensions: An Introduction
objectives: State that the x and the y coordinates are independent of each other.

misconceptions.claim: A ball thrown into the air travels in a curve because it is pushed sideways by the air.
misconceptions.correction: The curve comes from the two motions acting at once. The horizontal motion is steady, and the vertical motion is accelerated by gravity.

summary: The x and the y motions are independent.
Each one follows the rules of one dimensional motion.
The path of the object is the curve that the two together describe.

sections.title: Vector Addition and Subtraction: Graphical Methods
objectives: Add two vectors by drawing them head to tail and measuring the resultant.
Subtract a vector by adding its reverse.

misconceptions.claim: To subtract a vector, draw it again pointing the other way and add it.
misconceptions.correction: That is exactly right. The reverse of a vector has the same size and the opposite direction, so adding it is the subtraction.

summary: A vector is drawn as an arrow, with the tail at the starting point.
Vectors add head to tail, and the resultant runs from the first tail to the last head.

sections.title: Vector Addition and Subtraction: Analytical Methods
objectives: Resolve a vector into components and add the components separately.

misconceptions.claim: You have to add vectors by drawing them, there is no other way.
misconceptions.correction: Drawing works, but for numbers it is slow and imprecise. Resolving into components gives the same answer exactly.

summary: A vector can be broken into components along chosen axes.
The components are added one axis at a time, and then put back together.
The magnitude and the direction of the resultant follow from its components.

sections.title: Projectile Motion
objectives: Analyse a projectile by splitting its motion into horizontal and vertical parts.
Calculate the time of flight, the maximum height and the range of a projectile.

misconceptions.claim: The projectile keeps the speed it was launched with for the whole flight.
misconceptions.correction: The horizontal speed stays the same, because there is no horizontal force. The vertical speed changes every second, because gravity acts downward.

summary: The horizontal motion is uniform, the vertical motion is accelerated.
The time of flight is set by the vertical motion alone.
The maximum height is reached when the vertical velocity is zero.

sections.title: Addition of Velocities
objectives: Add the velocities of a moving frame and of an object to find the velocity seen by an observer.
Apply vector addition to relative velocity.

misconceptions.claim: If you run twice as fast on a moving train, you move twice as fast compared with the ground.
misconceptions.correction: Your speed compared with the train is unchanged, but compared with the ground the two velocities add.

summary: The velocity an observer measures is the sum of the object's velocity and the velocity of the frame.
The sum is a vector sum, so directions matter.
The same reasoning gives the relative velocity of two objects.

conditions.text: For motion in a plane, with the axes chosen for the problem.

definition.text: A quantity with both magnitude and direction, drawn as an arrow.
One of the parts a vector is broken into along a chosen axis.
The single vector that has the same effect as a set of vectors added together.
An object launched into the air and then moved only by gravity, with air resistance neglected.

The velocity of one object as seen from another, found by subtracting the two velocities as vectors.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: A projectile reaches its maximum range at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal.
exam_traps.correction: The range is greatest at 45 degrees, for the same launch speed on level ground.
exam_traps.signal: The paper offers 30 degrees as an option, and the answer is 45 degrees.

exam_recall_checks.subject: physics
exam_recall_checks.stem: A ball is projected horizontally at 20 m/s from a height of 45 m. How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take g = 10 m/s².)
exam_recall_checks.explanation: The vertical motion starts from rest, so h = ½gt² gives 45 = 5t², and t = 3 s. The horizontal speed does not change the time of the fall.
